data.name: Ayanir
data.gender_notes: Ayanir is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Ayanir is a Hindu name derived from the Sanskrit language. It is believed to be a name of the sky god, Indra. Ayanir represents power, intelligence, and the ability to overcome challenges. The name Ayanir carries the meaning “Sky God” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Tamil. Parents who choose Ayanir usually hope their child will grow to embody sky god and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Ayanir is a sacred name associated with the Hindu deity Indra, the god of the sky, rain, and thunder. It signifies strength, courage, and the power to conquer adversity.
data.etymology: Ayanir belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Sky God.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ayanir total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

Indra, the deity associated with the name, is the god of rain, thunderbolts, and the sky. In Hindu mythology, Indra is depicted as a warrior king who leads the devas (gods) in their battles against the asuras (demons). The name Ayanir is a reminder of the valor and courage that is deeply entwined within the Hindu tradition.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Ayanir holds deep spiritual significance for those who hold the Hindu faith. It symbolizes the power of the divine to help individuals overcome challenges and adversities in their lives. Indra, the deity associated with the name, is believed to bestow upon his devotees the strength and courage needed to face life's obstacles. Additionally, the name Ayanir is a reminder of the power and intelligence of the divine, and serves as a constant reminder of the interconnectedness and unity of all things in the universe.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Ayanir is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Ayan' which means 'wanderer' or 'pilgrim'. This name symbolizes the spiritual journey of the individual towards self-realization and enlightenment. The 'r' at the end signifies the goal of achieving union with the divine.

historical_references.reference: Ayanir is mentioned in the Mahabharata, an ancient Sanskrit epic that originated in India around the 4th century BCE. In one passage, Arjuna is described as invoking Ayanir to strike down his enemy Bhishma during the Kurukshetra war. The god is depicted as the lord of the northern direction and the ruler of the constellation of the bear Ursa Major.

Another reference to Ayanir can be found in the Puranas, a collection of ancient Hindu texts. In one of these texts, the Vayu Purana, Ayanir is described as one of the Vasus, a group of deities who protect and maintain the universe. He is also associated with the wind and the rain and is believed to bestow fertility and prosperity.
